criteria.descriptor: Full marks: correctly explains prefill-vs-decode and that decode is memory-bandwidth (not compute) bound, correctly attributes the 25% SM utilization / full HBM symptom, and describes continuous batching, PagedAttention/KV-cache limits, and quantization mechanisms accurately. Deduct for physical errors such as calling decode compute-bound, claiming a faster-FLOP GPU or lower temperature fixes utilization, or misstating what quantization/speculative decoding actually do.

Full marks: covers the diagnosis (two-phase + static-batching pathology + KV-cache limit) AND a prioritized multi-lever plan (continuous batching, paged KV, quantization, plus at least one of chunked prefill / speculative decoding / TP) AND the throughput-vs-latency SLO framing. Partial credit if it fixes throughput but ignores tail latency (or vice versa) or omits the KV-cache/memory dimension.

Full marks: each proposed change is justified by the mechanism (e.g. batching helps because it amortizes bandwidth-bound weight loads; quantization helps decode because it is bandwidth-bound) and its trade-off is stated. Deduct when recommendations are asserted as a checklist without linking cause to the observed symptoms or without acknowledging costs.

Full marks: well-organized (diagnosis then prioritized plan then trade-off), uses correct serving vocabulary precisely, and is concise. Deduct for disorganized dumps of buzzwords, vague hand-waving, or terminology used loosely/incorrectly.

expected_answer_points: Distinguishes prefill (parallel over prompt tokens, compute-bound GEMMs) from decode (one token/step, GEMV-like, low arithmetic intensity) and identifies decode as memory-bandwidth bound because weights + KV cache are streamed from HBM each step, explaining the low SM utilization despite full HBM.

Explains why static/padded batching hurts: wasted compute on padding, head-of-line blocking (short requests wait for the longest generation), and inability to admit new requests mid-flight, which inflates p99 tail latency.

Proposes continuous / in-flight batching (iteration-level scheduling, e.g. vLLM/Orca) so completed sequences leave and queued ones join, raising GPU utilization/throughput and cutting queueing latency.

Identifies the KV cache as the dominant memory consumer and true concurrency limit, and proposes PagedAttention-style block paging to remove fragmentation/over-reservation and increase concurrent sequences.

Proposes weight-only quantization (INT8/INT4, AWQ/GPTQ) and correctly ties the speedup to decode being bandwidth-bound (fewer bytes moved) plus freed memory for more KV cache, while noting the accuracy-risk trade-off and reduced benefit in compute-bound/large-batch regimes.

Articulates the core throughput-vs-latency trade-off: batching amortizes weight loads to boost throughput but raises per-request latency, so batch/concurrency must be tuned to the latency SLO rather than maximized blindly.

Adds at least one further appropriate lever with correct rationale (e.g. chunked prefill to stop long prefills stalling decode, speculative decoding for low-concurrency latency, or tensor parallelism) and mentions measuring prefill/decode latency, tokens/sec, SM util and KV occupancy separately.
common_pitfalls: Treats generation as one monolithic compute-bound operation and never separates prefill from decode, so cannot explain why SM utilization is low while HBM is full.
Diagnoses the low utilization as a compute shortfall and recommends a higher-FLOP GPU or more SMs, missing that bandwidth-bound decode is limited by HBM traffic, not FLOPs.

Suggests simply increasing the static batch size to raise throughput, ignoring that larger batches worsen per-request latency and that static batching's head-of-line blocking is the actual tail-latency cause.
Overlooks the KV cache entirely, assuming model weights are the only memory cost, and so cannot explain the concurrency ceiling or why PagedAttention helps.
Assumes weight-only INT4 quantization always yields a proportional speedup and ignores accuracy risk, dequant overhead, and its reduced benefit in the compute-bound large-batch regime.

Claims speculative decoding boosts aggregate throughput under high concurrency, missing that it primarily reduces latency at low batch and can waste compute on rejected draft tokens when the draft model is poorly aligned.
reference_answer:
Diagnosis. Autoregressive inference has two phases with opposite characteristics. Prefill processes all prompt tokens in parallel as large GEMMs and is compute-bound. Decode emits one token per sequence per step; the math is GEMV-like with very low arithmetic intensity, so each step is dominated by streaming the model weights (and the growing KV cache) out of HBM. Decode is therefore memory-bandwidth bound, which is exactly why SM utilization sits at ~25% while HBM is full: the GPU is waiting on memory, not compute. Static batching compounds this: padding every sequence to the batch maximum wastes compute, the whole batch is held until the slowest generation finishes (head-of-line blocking), and no new request can join mid-flight, so short requests queue behind 800-token generations, inflating p99. HBM being full points to the KV cache as the real concurrency limit.

Plan. (1) Switch to continuous/in-flight batching (vLLM/Orca): schedule at the iteration level so finished sequences exit and queued ones join every step. This raises effective batch size during decode, amortizing each weight load across more sequences, and removes head-of-line blocking, cutting tail latency. (2) Use PagedAttention so KV cache lives in fixed non-contiguous blocks; this eliminates fragmentation and max-length over-reservation, raising the number of concurrent sequences the 80GB can hold. (3) Apply weight-only quantization (INT8/INT4 via AWQ or GPTQ): because decode is bandwidth-bound, moving 4x fewer weight bytes directly speeds decode, and freed memory becomes more KV cache / concurrency. Trade-off: possible accuracy regression (validate on evals) and diminishing benefit in compute-bound, large-batch regimes. (4) Add chunked prefill so a 4000-token prefill is split and interleaved with ongoing decodes instead of stalling them. (5) For latency-sensitive, low-concurrency traffic, consider speculative decoding with a small draft model.

Trade-off framing. Batching maximizes throughput but raises per-request latency, so size max batch and max-num-seqs to the p99 SLO rather than blindly maximizing. Measure prefill vs decode latency, tokens/sec, SM utilization and KV-cache occupancy separately, and pick levers matched to whether the workload is latency- or throughput-bound.
